sections.h2: Where the Gaston County Register of Deeds is
sections.html:
You will find the office on the courthouse's first floor, 325 Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Way, Gastonia, NC 28052. Older deeds, letters and directions may show the former street name, 325 N. Marietta Street, for the same building.

Write to P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053, or phone 704-862-7681. Doors are open from 8:30 am to 5 pm. The 4:45 pm cutoff for real estate recordings falls before the office closes, so a late-afternoon closing in Gastonia, Belmont, Mount Holly or Cherryville should go in early. Using the records or taking a notary oath needs no appointment.

A new vendor now powers the records search, and the previous system is gone. All of its records moved to the new one, so any saved link to the old site should be replaced.

The public search finds deeds, deeds of trust and other property records. A few older records never went online, and the staff will help with those if you stop in or call. Uncertified copies can be pulled online. For a certified copy, use the Certified Copy Request Portal, call 704-862-7681, email rod@gastongov.com or go to the office. If you need a prior deed to prove how your family took title, you will usually want a certified copy for the closing attorney.

Beyond deeds, staff index plats, maps, mortgages and other personal property papers. The same counter issues marriage licenses, holds birth and death certificates and handles passport applications.

Paper records are kept in vaults, and digital copies sit on secure servers in the courthouse.

Plain copies run $0.25 a page. Certified copies start at $5 for page one, and each added page is $2.

Ways to pay Register of Deeds fees:

  • Cash.
  • Business check or money order payable to the Gaston County Register of Deeds.
  • Debit or credit card.

Employees can show you the books and help with the computers. State law keeps them from title research, and they will not run a lien check. If you lose a deed, buy a copy in person or write to the P.O. Box for one. A name change on a deed requires a brand new deed, so see an attorney, because the office stocks no legal forms for deeds or powers of attorney.

sections.h2: Recording fees for a closing package
sections.html:
The uniform fee schedule follows G.S. 161-10.

  • General instruments: $26 covers pages one to 15, then $4 per page.
  • Mortgages and deeds of trust: $64 covers pages one to 35, then the same $4 per page.
  • Satisfactions of a paid-off loan: free.
  • Plats: $21 for each sheet.
  • Additional instruments bundled in one document: $10 apiece.

The transfer tax comes on top. G.S. 105-228.30 sets it at one dollar for every $500 of price, rounding a remainder up to the next $500, and the seller pays when the deed is presented.

sections.h2: Timing your closing around the cutoff
sections.html:
The 4:45 pm recording cutoff is the date that matters most to a seller. A deed that arrives after it waits for the next business day, and during that gap an earlier filing by someone else can take priority. Ask your closing attorney or title agent to send the package well before the cutoff, and avoid scheduling signatures for the last hour of the day.

Have these ready when the package goes in: the signed deed, the fee payment, the transfer tax paid by you as seller, and the satisfaction for any loan being paid off. Payoff paperwork is recorded free, but it still needs to be filed. If you sell for cash, there may be no lender documents at all, and the package is shorter, though the deed and tax are the same.

Before you list, pull your own deed from the public search and read the legal description. If a name is misspelled or a prior owner never recorded a deed, tell your attorney right away, since fixing the chain takes longer than any other step. Ask for a certified copy only if the closing attorney requests one, because plain copies cost far less per page.

Questions about the county's land records can go to rod@gastongov.com, which is also the address for certified copy requests, so keep your parcel details handy when you write.

sections.h2: Protection from deed and lien fraud
sections.html:
A free alert service runs through the county's land records software provider. Enter a name and an email address, and a message arrives whenever a recording is filed under that name.

Alerts cannot stop fraud. They only let you notice a suspicious filing fast, which is valuable when the house is empty, rented or inherited and the mail piles up. People preparing documents for recording may not include Social Security, bank account or card numbers unless the law requires one. A number that slips through can be taken off the online image if you ask in writing under G.S. 132-1.10(g). That request is free, but the filing itself stays public.

sections.h2: How values and appeals tie to a sale
sections.html:
A four-year reappraisal cycle applies here. January 1, 2023 is the latest value date, and 2027 is next, with an informal review ahead of any Board of Equalization and Review hearing.

Appeals can be filed beginning January 1 and ending when the board adjourns, usually the last week of April, or 30 days after a Notice of Value Change when that comes later. Reach the Tax Office at 128 West Main Avenue in Gastonia or 704-866-3158. The Register of Deeds does not collect property tax. That bill stays with the parcel until paid, and buyers expect it cleared at closing. Our Gaston County property tax guide covers rates, relief programs and payment options in detail.

The first paper registered usually ranks first. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance or a lease of more than three years has no effect on lien creditors or paying buyers until it is on record in the county where the land lies.

Before the buyer's deed is filed, make sure the earlier deeds in the chain, any estate documents and the release of a paid-off loan are all indexed. Recording a release costs nothing. Your closing attorney can search the index and send in the satisfaction of your old mortgage before the sale.

sections.h2: What an heir should record before selling
sections.html:
Estate paperwork comes first, because a deed signed by someone not yet holding title will not clear. When a small estate has no will, G.S. 28A-25-1 allows a small estate affidavit, filed where the decedent lived.

It covers up to $20,000 in personal property after liens, and the affidavit names every tract of land the decedent owned. Whichever route your family uses, the document giving you authority to sell ends up in the Gastonia index, so leave time before closing.

faqs.q: What is the mailing address for Gaston County recordings?
faqs.a: Address the envelope to Gaston County Register of Deeds, P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053. If you ship overnight, use an express envelope and enclose a prepaid return envelope.

faqs.q: How late in the day can a Gaston County deed be filed?
faqs.a: 4:45 pm for real estate recordings. The office stays open until 5 pm, but marriage applications stop at 4:30 pm.

faqs.q: How much are copies at the Gaston County office?
faqs.a: A black and white copy is $0.25 a page. A certified copy is $5 for the first page and $2 for every page after it.

faqs.q: Is the Gaston County records search online?
faqs.a: Yes, through a public search, and nothing was lost in the switch to the new vendor. A few older records are not digitized, so phone 704-862-7681 if you cannot find one.

faqs.q: Is the Gaston County deed tax the buyer's or the seller's?
faqs.a: You do, as the seller, at one dollar for each $500 of price when the deed is handed in. Your settlement statement shows the exact figure.
